title: Cluster brightness and EV indicators
body: Park safely, then check the vehicle screen and cluster directly. This guide covers brightness, READY, service and power-down indicators only. CarCue neither reads these indicator sensors nor controls brightness, and does not diagnose faults or determine whether driving is safe.

steps.title: Adjust brightness while parked
steps.body: With the vehicle ON, open Settings > Display > Screen brightness on its infotainment system. Adjust manually or select automatic day/night brightness, which follows ambient light. Cluster and infotainment brightness change together. With the position lights on, interior switch lighting is also adjusted.

steps.title: Distinguish READY from the service warning
steps.body: READY lights after startup when driving preparation is complete. Off means normal driving is unavailable; flashing means emergency operation. The service warning lights with ON, then goes out after 3 seconds.
official_cautions: If READY is off or flashing after startup, have a nearby Hyundai High-tech Center or Bluehands inspect and service the vehicle.
If the service warning lights while driving or stays on after startup, have a nearby Hyundai High-tech Center or Bluehands inspect and service the vehicle.

steps.title: Check the power-down cautions
steps.body: Power-down indicates output restriction to protect high-power components. It may appear with very low charge or falling voltage in the high-voltage battery, or high drive-system temperature. The manual does not describe power-down alone as a fault.
official_cautions: If power-down and the service warning light together, have a Hyundai High-tech Center or Bluehands inspect the vehicle.
Do not accelerate sharply or make a sudden start while power-down is lit.
Restricted output can make climbing a slope difficult or allow the vehicle to roll back on a slope.
